::: {.hero-text}
# Lidio Jaimes Jr {.hero-name}

[Biostatistics Sc.M. -- Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health]{.hero-tagline}

I'm a biostatistics master's student at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, graduating in May 2027. I hold a B.S. in Statistics from the University of Georgia.

At Johns Hopkins Medicine, I work on three cystic fibrosis studies, developing R pipelines to automate study reports and performing quality control and assurance on longitudinal patient health data. I'm also a graduate research assistant studying cognitive aging in older adults using data from the National Health and Aging Trends Study. This academic year, I'm serving as a teaching assistant for four courses in the Department of Biostatistics.

Before Hopkins, I conducted research at the University of Georgia, UC Irvine, and Columbia University on stroke outcomes, Alzheimer's disease in individuals with Down syndrome, and Medicare costs associated with lung cancer, respectively. I work primarily in R, Python, SAS, and SQL.

:::
:::

### Predictors of stroke severity

[Alzheimer's & Down syndrome]{.card-kicker}

### Neuropsychiatric symptoms and emerging dementia

Longitudinal analysis of 1,274 Down syndrome and 183,097 late-onset Alzheimer's visits. Co-author on the resulting paper in *Alzheimer's & Dementia* (2025).

[Read more →](research.qmd#nps-in-alzheimers)
